knitr::opts_chunk$set(

## 1. Data Preparation and Structure

```{r load-data}
# 1. Load required libraries
library(nlmm)
library(tidyverse)
library(rstatix)
library(ggpubr)

# 2. Load dataset
data("rats", package = "nlmm")

# 3. Format factor variables with clear labels
rats <- rats %>%
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),
    trt = factor(
      trt,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c("Control", "Thiouracil", "Thyroxin")
    ),
    time = factor(
      time,
      levels = 0:4,
      labels = c("Week 0", "Week 1", "Week 2", "Week 3", "Week 4")
    )
  )

# 4. Inspect data structure
str(rats)
dim(rats)
head(rats)
table(rats$trt)
```

## 2. Descriptive Statistics and Visualizations

```{r descriptive-stats}
rats %>%
  group_by(trt, time) %>%
  get_summary_stats(y, type = "mean_sd")
```

```{r boxplot}
# Boxplot across time points by treatment group
ggboxplot(
  rats,
  x = "time",
  y = "y",
  color = "trt",
  palette = "jco",
  add = "jitter"
) +
  labs(
    title = "Body Weight Distribution Across Weeks by Treatment",
    x = "Measurement Occasion",
    y = "Body Weight (grams)",
    color = "Treatment"
  )
```

```{r interaction-plot}
# Interaction plot of mean body weights over time
rats %>%
  group_by(trt, time) %>%
  summarise(mean_weight = mean(y), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time, y = mean_weight, color = trt, group = trt)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Growth Trajectories by Treatment Group",
    x = "Measurement Occasion",
    y = "Mean Body Weight (grams)",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 3. Assumption Checks

```{r normality-test}
# Shapiro-Wilk test per Treatment x Time combination
rats %>%
  group_by(trt, time) %>%
  shapiro_test(y)
```

```{r outlier-detection}
# Identify univariate outliers per Treatment x Time cell (mild and extreme)
rats %>%
  group_by(trt, time) %>%
  identify_outliers(y)
```

```{r levene-test}
# Conduct Levene's test at each measurement occasion
rats %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  levene_test(y ~ trt)
```

```{r box-m-test}
# Reshape data to wide format for Box's M test
rats_wide <- rats %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(id, trt),
    names_from = time,
    values_from = y,
    names_prefix = "time_"
  )

# Perform Box's M test (evaluate at alpha = 0.001)
box_m(
  rats_wide %>% select(starts_with("time_")),
  rats_wide$trt
)
```

## 4. Mixed-Design Repeated Measures ANOVA

```{r mixed-anova}
# Fit mixed ANOVA
res.aov <- anova_test(
  data = rats,
  dv = y,
  wid = id,
  between = trt,
  within = time
)

# Display complete ANOVA and Sphericity output
res.aov

# Extract formatted ANOVA table
get_anova_table(res.aov)
```

## 5. Simple Main Effects and Post-Hoc Comparisons

```{r simple-main-treatment}
# One-way ANOVA per time point
rats %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  anova_test(dv = y, wid = id, between = trt) %>%
  get_anova_table() %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons per week (all 15 rows across 5 weeks x 3 pairs)
rats %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  tukey_hsd(y ~ trt) %>%
  select(time, group1, group2, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.adj, p.adj.signif) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r simple-main-time}
# Repeated measures ANOVA per treatment group
rats %>%
  group_by(trt) %>%
  anova_test(dv = y, wid = id, within = time) %>%
  get_anova_table()

# Paired t-tests between weeks with Holm correction (adjusted within each treatment group)
rats %>%
  group_by(trt) %>%
  pairwise_t_test(
    y ~ time,
    paired = TRUE,
    p.adjust.method = "holm"
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## 6. APA Results Summary

A two-way mixed-design repeated measures ANOVA was conducted to examine the effects of treatment group (Control, Thiouracil, Thyroxin; between-subjects) and measurement occasion (Week 0 to Week 4; within-subjects) on rat body weight ($N = 27$ rats across $135$ observations). Because Mauchly's test indicated violations of sphericity ($W = 0.011$, $p < .001$), Greenhouse–Geisser corrected degrees of freedom are reported for within-subjects effects.

* **Treatment $\times$ Time Interaction:** $F(2.73, 32.82) = 16.59$, $p < .001$, $\eta_G^2 = .31$
* **Main Effect of Treatment:** $F(2.00, 24.00) = 7.88$, $p = .002$, $\eta_G^2 = .31$
* **Main Effect of Time:** $F(1.37, 32.82) = 745.92$, $p < .001$, $\eta_G^2 = .91$

Follow-up simple main effects showed no significant differences in body weight among treatment groups at Week 0, $F(2, 24) = 0.24$, $p = .792$, $\eta_G^2 = .02$; Week 1, $F(2, 24) = 0.27$, $p = .769$, $\eta_G^2 = .02$; or Week 2, $F(2, 24) = 3.17$, $p = .060$, $\eta_G^2 = .21$. Significant group differences emerged by Week 3, $F(2, 24) = 10.04$, $p = .001$, $\eta_G^2 = .46$, and persisted through Week 4, $F(2, 24) = 17.80$, $p < .001$, $\eta_G^2 = .60$, where Tukey HSD post-hoc tests indicated that the Thiouracil group had significantly lower mean body weight than both the Control and Thyroxin groups ($p_{\text{adj}} \le .002$ at Week 3; $p_{\text{adj}} < .001$ at Week 4), while Control and Thyroxin did not differ significantly ($p_{\text{adj}} \ge .912$). Within each treatment group, body weight increased significantly over time for Control, $F(1.32, 11.90) = 399.00$, $p < .001$, $\eta_G^2 = .93$, Thiouracil, $F(1.77, 15.90) = 225.00$, $p < .001$, $\eta_G^2 = .90$, and Thyroxin, $F(1.15, 6.91) = 161.00$, $p < .001$, $\eta_G^2 = .90$.
